newsitem.title: HONG KONG: OLS trades below issue price on debut.
newsitem.headline: OLS trades below issue price on debut.

text.p: Shares of OLS Group Ltd traded below their issue price in their market debut on Thursday, with brokers saying interest was limited by a lack of excitement for construction stocks and a labour dispute involving the company.
OLS shares were at HK$1.40 at midday after opening at HK$1.69. The shares were issued at HK$1.65.
Volume was 19.97 million shares worth HK$28.68 million.
Brokers said a labour dispute involving the company had helped to dampen buying interest.
"It was seen to have a psychological impact on investors, resulting in limited buying interest for the stock," said a sales manager at a regional brokerage.

About 40 labourers who worked on the Hong Kong Convention Centre Extension where Britain's Prince Charles will hand back the territory to Chinese President Jiang Zemin at midnight on June 30 gathered at the site on Wednesday to demand back pay.
The workers said they were owed some HK$10 million for interior painting, panelling and glass work.
OLS said in a statement on Thursday it was not involved in the dispute and had made payment to sub-contractors in accordance with the progress of the project.
"We did not withhold wages," OLS said in the statement.
Analysts said investors rushing to liquidate positions ahead of the long market holiday to mark the handover and a general lack of interest in construction stocks also triggered selling.

"Construction stocks are not that exciting to local investors and its P/E (price to earnings multiple) is also seen to be unattractive to investors," said Pamela Lam, an analyst at Pacific Challenge Securities.
Analysts said OLS offered its shares at a P/E of 7.6 percent on a fully-diluted basis, almost the same as other construction concerns.
OLS Group, a unit of OLS Asia Holdings Ltd, offered 120 million new shares.
The 108 million shares offered to the Hong Kong public were about 16.95 times subscribed, while the 12 million shares for company employees were fully allotted.
